questions.q: What command confirms Git installed correctly?
options: git --version
git install --check
git status --confirm
git verify
questions.explain: git --version prints the installed Git version, like "git version 2.46.0", confirming the install worked.

questions.q: Why do you set user.name and user.email with git config --global before committing?
options: Every commit is permanently stamped with this name and email, and --global applies it to every repository on your machine
It's required only for the very first commit and never matters again
It changes the color scheme of the terminal
It uploads your credentials to GitHub automatically
questions.explain: Git attributes every commit you ever make to this name and email; --global sets it once for all repositories instead of per-project.

questions.q: What does git init actually do to a folder of existing .sql files?
options: It creates a hidden .git folder alongside the files, turning the folder into a repository, without changing the files themselves
It deletes all existing files and starts a blank project
It uploads the folder to GitHub immediately
It renames all .sql files to .git files
questions.explain: git init only adds a .git subfolder that holds the repository's data — your actual .sql files are untouched.

questions.q: After running git init and then git status in a folder with untracked .sql files, what would you expect to see?
options: Git reports it sees the files but isn't tracking them yet
Git reports the files are already committed
Git throws an error because .sql files aren't supported
Git automatically commits every file it finds
questions.explain: Right after git init, Git recognizes untracked files in the working directory but has not staged or committed them — that's the starting point Lesson 3 builds on.

questions.q: What does the --global flag do on git config?
options: Applies the setting to every repository on your machine, not just the current one
Publishes your Git config to a public server
Only applies the setting for the next single command
Deletes any existing Git configuration
questions.explain: --global writes the setting to your machine-wide Git config, so you don't have to repeat it in every new repository.
